items.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Supply Chain Attack
points: Ledger's Donjon security team discovered unauthorized LTE/eSIM components hidden in devices sold by reseller CryptoBilis, which intercepted and transmitted users' 24-word recovery phrases (security codes used to restore crypto wallets) during setup.
The implant targeted the visible setup process rather than Ledger's protected Secure Element (a hardened chip storing private keys), so core cryptographic protections remained intact.
An estimated $86 million in cryptocurrency was drained from affected wallets; a modified device was also found sold in Germany via reseller MediaMarkt Saturn, prompting sales halts.
Trezor and other competitors are cutting authorized reseller networks and issuing reassurance statements, reflecting industry-wide concern about supply chain vulnerabilities beyond Ledger.

items.title: UK Court Rules on Seized $5B Bitcoin Haul
points: UK High Court ruled that Chinese law governs claims to 61,000 BTC (currently worth about $5 billion) seized from suspected money launderer Zhimin Qian.
The ruling makes it harder for fraud victims to recover stolen assets deposited in the UK, favoring the government's ability to retain the seized Bitcoin.

items.title: France Proposes Crypto Holdings Disclosure Rule
points: France proposed requiring crypto owners to disclose holdings exceeding €100,000 (about $112,000).

The proposal has sparked privacy and security backlash, especially following a pattern of violent home invasions known as 'wrench attacks,' where criminals use physical force to extract crypto access codes from victims.

headlines: Ledger confirms hardware wallets sold via Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden LTE implants that could steal recovery phrases (24-word security codes used to restore wallets), with suspected $86M in losses.
Trezor is cutting its reseller network and other manufacturers issuing reassurance statements after the Ledger supply chain compromise, heightening concerns about unauthorized hardware modifications.
UK court ruling favors government keeping $5 billion Bitcoin haul seized from Zhimin Qian by applying Chinese law to fraud victims' claims against the assets.
France's proposed requirement for crypto owners to report holdings over €100,000 sparks backlash over privacy concerns following recent violent physical theft attacks (wrench attacks).

sections.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Supply Chain Attack
points: 1. Ledger's Donjon security team discovered unauthorized LTE/eSIM components in devices sold by CryptoBilis that intercepted and transmitted 24-word recovery phrases as users entered them during wallet setup.
2. The implant targeted the visible setup process, not Ledger's protected Secure Element (a hardened chip storing private keys), meaning the core cryptographic protection remained intact.

3. An estimated $86 million in cryptocurrency was drained from affected wallets, and Ledger confirmed a modified device was also sold in Germany through reseller MediaMarkt Saturn, prompting sales halts.

4. Trezor and other competitors are cutting authorized resellers and issuing reassurances as a precautionary measure, indicating industry-wide concern about supply chain vulnerabilities beyond Ledger.
